title: Pointwise reflections assemble to coherent adjunctions for full inclusions
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, transformations, full subcategories and mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and canonical mapping-space composition from [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Work in a fixed containing universe. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory and $i:\mathcal D\hookrightarrow\mathcal C$ the inclusion of a full subcategory. Suppose that every $x\in\mathcal C$ admits an edge $u_x:x\to i(d_x)$ with $d_x\in\mathcal D$, such that precomposition induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(i(d_x),i(d))\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,i(d))$ for every $d\in\mathcal D$. Then there exist a coherent functor $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and coherent transformations $a:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}\to iP$, $b:Pi\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ satisfying the triangle identities up to homotopy in the corresponding functor quasicategories. Every component $a_x$ has the stated universal precomposition property. The dual assertion holds: if every $x$ admits $v_x:i(d_x)\to x$ inducing equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(i(d),i(d_x))\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(i(d),x)$ for all $d\in\mathcal D$, then there are $B:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $c:iB\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ and $e:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}\to Bi$ with coherent triangle homotopies, and every $c_x$ has this universal postcomposition property. No compatibility of the initially supplied objectwise witnesses is assumed.

source.place: Kerodon 02FD, Lemma 6.2.2.23, and 02FE, Proposition 6.2.2.24, with their coreflective duals. Read online 2026-10-17, not archived; these are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Form the full simplicial subcategory $E\subseteq\mathcal C\times\Delta^1$ on $(x,0)$ for $x\in\mathcal C$ and $(i(d),1)$ for $d\in\mathcal D$, and let $p:E\to\Delta^1$ be the projection. It is an inner fibration. Indeed an inner horn in $E$ projects to a horn in $\mathcal C$, which has a filler; pair that filler with the prescribed simplex in $\Delta^1$. Every vertex already belongs to $E$, so fullness puts the paired filler in $E$. The same horn argument makes $E$ a quasicategory. The fibers are $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$. Directly from the right-pinched definition, $\operatorname{Map}_E((x,0),(i(d),1))=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,i(d))$, the mapping spaces within the two fibers are their own mapping spaces, and all mapping spaces from fiber $1$ to fiber $0$ are empty. In the cocartesian mapping-square criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], a lift $\widetilde u:(x,0)\to(i(d_x),1)$ of a supplied $u_x$ has, for a test vertex in fiber $1$, two singleton base mapping spaces and precisely the hypothesized equivalence as its top map. For a test vertex in fiber $0$, the bottom left and top left corners are empty and the bottom right is a singleton, so its homotopy pullback is empty. Thus every supplied $u_x$ gives a $p$-cocartesian edge. This calculation also proves that any $p$-cocartesian mixed edge has exactly the universal precomposition property in the item.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.2.23, full subcategory E and its mixed cocartesian edges; the horn and mapping-space checks are expanded here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-arrow-projection] to this inner fibration $p$, using its notation $Y,Z,\theta$. The fixed base edge $\alpha:0\to1$ defines a simplicial map $t:\mathcal C\to Z$, $x\mapsto(\alpha,(x,0))$: in every degree its first coordinate is the constant simplex at $\alpha$, and its second coordinate is the fiber inclusion. It lands in the full vertex image $Z$ by Step 1 and the objectwise hypotheses. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to the trivial Kan fibration $\theta$ and the degreewise injective inclusion $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\mathcal C$. This gives a simplicial lift $h:\mathcal C\to Y$ with $\theta h=t$. Uncurrying gives $H:\mathcal C\times\Delta^1\to E$ whose initial restriction is the fiber inclusion, whose final restriction takes values in the full fiber $\mathcal D$, and whose vertical edges are $p$-cocartesian. The endpoint and first projection therefore give $P:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $a:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}\to iP$. The last sentence of Step 1 supplies the universal precomposition equivalence for every $a_x$. The whole lift is simplicial, so $P$ and $a$ already contain all their naturality parameters. The supplied witnesses were used only to show that the vertices of $t$ lie in $Z$.

source.place: Lemma 6.2.2.23, assembly step, expanded via the trivial Kan fibration in the cocartesian dual of Proposition 5.2.1.3 (01VK).

proof.text: Restrict $a$ to $\mathcal D$. For $d\in\mathcal D$, fullness identifies the universal map with precomposition $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Pi(d),z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(d,z)$ for every $z\in\mathcal D$. At $z=d$, its surjectivity on components gives $b_d:Pi(d)\to d$ with $b_d a_{i(d)}\simeq1_d$. At $z=Pi(d)$, injectivity on components, applied after precomposition with $a_{i(d)}$, gives $a_{i(d)}b_d\simeq1_{Pi(d)}$. The inverse criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] makes $a_{i(d)}$ an equivalence. The restriction of $a$ is an edge $a_D:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}\to Pi$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal D,\mathcal D)$: its simplices lie there because all their vertices lie in the full subcategory $\mathcal D$. The componentwise criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes this edge an equivalence. Choose its inverse $b:Pi\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$ in that functor quasicategory, with both inverse homotopies. In particular $i b\circ a i\simeq1_i$ is a homotopy of coherent transformations, giving the first triangle.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.2.24, reflection arrows on the full subcategory are equivalences; counit obtained as a coherent inverse.

proof.text: Naturality of $a$ at $a_x$ gives $(iP(a_x))a_x\simeq a_{iP(x)}a_x$. Both right-hand factors after $a_x$ have target $iPiP(x)$ in $i(\mathcal D)$. The injectivity on components of the universal precomposition equivalence for $a_x$ therefore gives $iP(a_x)\simeq a_{iP(x)}$. The latter is an equivalence by Step 3; fullness and the inverse criterion for component classes show that $P(a_x)$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal D$. Consequently $Pa:P\to PiP$ is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal D)$ by the componentwise criterion. Also $bP$ is an equivalence, since its inverse and inverse homotopies are obtained by precomposing the inverse data for $b$ with $P$. Thus the composite $\beta=bP\circ Pa$ is invertible in the homotopy category of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal D)$. This step only uses objectwise cancellation to prove invertibility; the coherent equality $\beta\simeq1_P$ is proved in Step 5.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.2.24, proof of (2) implies (3): naturality at the unit edge makes P(a_x) an equivalence.

proof.text:
Do the following calculation in the homotopy categories of the full functor quasicategories; juxtaposition of transformations means vertical composition, with the rightmost applied first. Whiskering is restriction or postcomposition of the internal functor simplicial sets. The spine calculus [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] supplies composition and its homotopies. The interchange equalities used below come from the two triangles of an evaluation square: for transformations $r:F\to G$ and $s:H\to J$, evaluate $s$ on $r$ as a map with two $\Delta^1$ factors; the two routes around that square have the same diagonal composite. This is an equality in the homotopy category of the entire functor object, retaining its diagram parameter. Applying it to $Pa$ and $b$, to $b$ and itself, and to $a$ and itself (then applying $P$) gives, respectively,
$$Pa\,bP=bPiP\,PiPa,\qquad bP\,bPiP=bP\,Pi bP,\qquad PiPa\,Pa=Pa iP\,Pa.$$
Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta^2&=bP\,Pa\,bP\,Pa\\
&=bP\,bPiP\,PiPa\,Pa\\
&=bP\,Pi bP\,Pa iP\,Pa\\
&=bP\,P(i bP\,a iP)\,Pa\\
&=bP\,Pa=\beta.
\end{aligned}$$
The penultimate equality uses the first triangle from Step 3 whiskered by $P$ on both sides. Since $\beta$ is invertible by Step 4, $\beta^2=\beta$ implies $\beta=1_P$. An equality of these morphism classes is a path between the corresponding vertices in the mapping Kan complex of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal D)$, so this is the required coherent second triangle homotopy. This explicitly proves both triangles without inferring natural homotopy from pointwise homotopy.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.4.6 (02DK), proof via the invertible idempotent triangle defect, expanded as a whiskering calculation.

proof.text: For the dual assertion apply Steps 1--5 to $i^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}\hookrightarrow\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Explicitly reversal keeps the $n$-simplices and replaces every simplicial operator $\gamma:[m]\to[n]$ by $\rho_n\gamma\rho_m$, where $\rho_j(t)=j-t$. This exchanges inner horns with inner horns and reverses every edge. The arrow-space comparison [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] identifies the given mapping spaces with the arrow mapping spaces $U$. Reversing the interval identifies $U_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)$ with $U_{\mathcal C}(y,x)^{\mathrm{op}}$; reversing the barycentric coordinates identifies the realizations of a simplicial set and its opposite. Thus weak equivalences are preserved. Reversal of the composition triangles in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] exchanges postcomposition by $v_x$ with precomposition by $v_x^{\mathrm{op}}$. The dual hypotheses are consequently precisely those of the reflective construction in the opposite categories. It gives $P':\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$ with unit $a'$ and counit $b'$. Reversing back yields $B=(P')^{\mathrm{op}}$, $c=(a')^{\mathrm{op}}:iB\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ and $e=(b')^{\mathrm{op}}:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}\to Bi$. The triangle homotopies reverse to $c i\circ i e\simeq1_i$ and $Bc\circ eB\simeq1_B$ in the full functor quasicategories; the same mapping-space comparison gives the required postcomposition property for every $c_x$. No compatibility among the original witnesses is needed in either construction.
